about: One record per external specification, standards draft or vendor document that a delivered connector adapter depends on, plus the Ceremony-internal profile identifiers the ledgers cite so that every `sourceProfileIds` entry resolves. Records are drawn from the swarm ledgers under ./ledger/; the `recordedBy` field names the ledger that pinned the facts. Licence fields say exactly how the licence was established; `not-read-here` means nobody in this execution read the licence and no reuse beyond citation is claimed. No external manual is copied into this repository: adapters restate wire facts (paths, field names, header names, documented constraints) and cite the document.
rules: A digest identifies bytes. It is not trust, not authorization and not a certification.

An SDK's open-source licence does not license the vendor's catalog assets: app names, logos, marks, category data, connector catalogs, icon sets and curated app lists are separately owned and are neither redistributed nor embedded by any adapter here.
Where a document is a draft, the exact draft revision is recorded and no finalized-standard or certified claim is made anywhere.
Where a vendor publishes no operation for an intended lifecycle action, the adapter records the native limitation. No endpoint is invented to fill a gap in a document.
Every record's facts were read from the document itself. No record here is evidence that a live account, a paid plan or a provider certification exists.

licence.statement: See rfc9700.

records.reuse: A strict scanner over the document text detects duplicate keys before JSON.parse collapses them, and bounds depth, node count, key and string lengths.
records.notes: JSON.parse silently keeps the last member and a reviver runs only after the collapse, which is why the scanner exists.

records.title: YAML 1.2 specification, core schema

licence.statement: The YAML specification's licence was not read here. No specification text is copied.

records.reuse: YAML is read only as YAML 1.2 with the core schema. An explicit %YAML 1.1 directive is refused rather than reinterpreted, because 1.1 changes the meaning of unquoted yes/no/on/off and of sexagesimal scalars.
records.notes: Explicit !!binary, !!timestamp, !!omap, !!set and !!pairs tags are refused; merge keys (<<) are refused rather than applied; a multi-document stream is refused instead of silently using the first document.

records.title: Node.js 22 DNS resolution behaviour
records.upstreamVersion: Node 22.22.2 in this environment; >=22.12 engine, Node 24 documented target

licence.status: Node.js documentation licence (MIT for the project)
licence.statement: Not read here; no documentation text is copied.

records.reuse: Lookup behaviour is what makes DNS-rebinding defence possible: the address check is bound to the answers the socket actually uses.
records.notes: Named limitation: a loopback fixture binds to 127.0.0.0/8, which classifies as loopback rather than private, so an end-to-end connection to an administrator-approved private origin cannot be demonstrated offline.
